annotations.title: Holy ground.
annotations.text: [1] If that apparition of God him ſelf or an Angel, could make the place and ground holy, and to be vſed of Moyſes with al ſignes of reuerence and feare: [2] how much more the corporal birth, abode, and wonders of the Sonne of God in Ievvrie, and his perſonal preſence in the B. Sacrament, may make that countrie and al Chriſtian Churches & altars holy? And it is the greateſt blindnes that can be, to thinke it ſuperſtition to reuerence any things or places in reſpect of Gods preſence or wonderous operation in the ſame. See S. Hierom. ep. 17. 18. 27. of the holy land.

annotations.title: Not in houſes.
annotations.text: The vulgar Heretikes alleage this place againſt the corporal being of Chriſt in the B. Sacrament & in Churches: by which reaſon they might haue driuen him out of al houſes, Churches, and corporal places, when he vvas viſible in earth. But it is meant of the Diuinitie only, & ſpoken to correct the carnal Ievves: <mn>◦</mn> Who thought God either ſo to be conteined, compaſſed, and limited to their Temple, that he could be no vvhere els, or at leaſt that he vvould not heare or receiue mens praiers and ſacrifices in the Churches of the Gentiles, or els vvhere, out of the ſaid Temple. And ſo as it maketh nothing for the Sacramentaries, no more doth it ſerue for ſuch as eſteeme Churches and places of publike praier no more conuenient nor more holy then any other profane houſes or chambers. For though his perſon or vertue be not limited to any place, yet it pleaſeth him condeſcending to our neceſſitie and profite, to vvorke his vvonders and to be vvorſhipped of vs in holy places rather then profane.

notes.text: God is not conteined in place, yet he vvil be vvorshipped in one place more then in an other.

annotations.title: They ſtoned him.
annotations.text: Read a maruelous narration in S. Auguſtine of one ſtone, that hitting the Martyr on the elbow, rebounded backe to a faithful man that ſtood near. ◦ Who keeping and carying it vvith him, vvas by reuelation vvarned to leaue it at Ancona in Italie: whereupon a Church or Memory of S. Steuen vvas there erected, and many miracles done after the ſaid Martyr's body was found out, and not before. Aug. to. 10. ſer. 38. de diuerſis in edit. Pariſ.
